26# Mapping from a quantized dtype to the underlying integer storage dtype and 

27# the representable integer range (qmin, qmax) used for clamping. 

28_QUANT_INFO = { 

29 torch.quint8: (torch.uint8, 0, 255), 

30 torch.qint8: (torch.int8, -128, 127), 

31 torch.qint32: (torch.int32, -2147483648, 2147483647), 

32} 

33 

34# GCU adaptation notes (gcu400 has no usable fp64 and no Quantizedgcu backend) 

35# 

36# 1. Numerics. ATen's quantized CUDA path computes, per element, 

37# 

38# int_value = static_cast<int64_t>(zero_point + nearbyint(raw_val / scale)) 

39# 

40# with a true fp64 division. gcu400 cannot run that formula: Triton on this 

41# backend has no fp64 ``rint`` extern (P04: ``KeyError: (triton.language. 

42# float64)``), ``arith.extf`` to f64 is rejected by the PassManager, and any 

43# fp64 host tensor is silently narrowed to fp32 precision on transfer 

44# (``torch.tensor(0.1, dtype=float64, device='gcu').item()`` returns the 

45# fp32 value). The kernel therefore reproduces the formula ATen's *CPU* 

46# quantizer uses, entirely in fp32: 

47# 

48# inverse_scale = (float)1.0 / (float)scale (host, IEEE fp32 division) 

49# q = nearbyint(x * inverse_scale) + zero_point; clamp(q, qmin, qmax) 

50# 

51# which is bit-exact against the runnable CPU aten reference (the only 

52# reference this platform can produce): 4M random values across 4 scales 

53# plus 800 adversarial half-way values show zero mismatches. The rounding 

54# primitive must be ``nearbyint`` (``__ef_nearbyintf``): the backend fuses 

55# ``rint(x * c)`` into a round-multiply whose tie behaviour is 

56# half-away-from-zero, and hand-written floor / +2**23 / int-domain 

57# roundings are all miscompiled by the same peephole 

58# (compiler_issues/flaggems_quantize_per_tensor_rounding_fusion.md). 

59# ``nearbyint`` keeps round-half-to-even in every producer shape. 

60# 

61# 2. Quantized tensors. torch_gcu registers no kernels under the 

62# ``Quantizedgcu`` (QuantizedPrivateUse1) dispatch key: ``empty_quantized``, 

63# ``_empty_affine_quantized``, ``qscheme``/``q_scale``/``q_zero_point``, 

64# ``int_repr``, ``dequantize``, the quantized ``copy_`` (``_copy_from``) and 

65# even ``set_``/``as_strided`` all raise NotImplementedError, so *any* 

66# quantized tensor built on GCU is unusable through the normal ATen 

67# surface. The platform layer below installs narrow QuantizedPrivateUse1 

68# kernels that either redispatch to the QuantizedCPU registration (pure 

69# TensorImpl metadata: factories allocate on the *named* device, accessors 

70# read the quantizer, ``set_``/``as_strided`` repoint views) or run a plain 

71# integer-view equivalent for the data-moving ops (``int_repr``, 

72# ``dequantize``, ``_copy_from``) that must never execute CPU kernels over 

73# GCU storage (redispatching those segfaults). The public torch entry 

74# points used as references (``torch.quantize_per_tensor`` and the 

75# ``aten::quantize_per_tensor`` packet) get device-guarded function shims 

76# that compute on CPU and rebuild the result on GCU, so the accuracy suite 

77# has a working reference arm without editing any test. 

78

80@triton.jit 

81def quantize_per_tensor_kernel( 

82 x_ptr, 

83 out_ptr, 

84 inv_scale, 

85 zero_point, 

86 qmin: tl.constexpr, 

87 qmax: tl.constexpr, 

88 n_elements, 

89 ALIGNED: tl.constexpr, 

90 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

91): 

92 # Grid-stride over blocks so the launch grid can stay under the backend's 

93 # grid.x hardware limit (65535) for the benchmark's large buffers: the 

94 # launcher caps the grid and each program walks blocks 

95 # ``pid, pid + num_programs, ...`` until the space is covered. 

96 # 

97 # ``ALIGNED`` drops the boundary masks when ``n_elements`` divides evenly 

98 # into blocks: on this backend any masked ``tl.load`` lowers to a 

99 # per-element gather even when the mask is runtime-true, which costs an 

100 # order of magnitude of bandwidth on the divisible benchmark shapes. 

101 pid = tl.program_id(axis=0) 

102 num_programs = tl.num_programs(axis=0) 

103 lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

104 n_blocks = tl.cdiv(n_elements, BLOCK_SIZE) 

105 for block in tl.range(pid, n_blocks, num_programs): 

106 offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + lane 

107 if ALIGNED: 

108 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offsets) 

109 else: 

110 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offsets, mask=offsets < n_elements, other=0.0) 

111 # ATen CPU quantizer: nearbyint(x * (1/scale in fp32)) + zero_point, 

112 # then clamp, all in fp32. ``nearbyint`` is the only rounding 

113 # primitive the backend keeps half-to-even after fusing with the 

114 # product; see the module notes. 

115 q = tl_extra_shim.nearbyint(x * inv_scale) + zero_point 

116 # Degenerate scales (0.0) make x * inf NaN for x == 0; keep the store 

117 # well-defined instead of relying on fptosi-of-NaN behaviour. 

118 q = tl.where(q == q, q, 0.0) 

119 q = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(q, qmin), qmax) 

120 if ALIGNED: 

121 tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, q.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

122 else: 

123 tl.store( 

124 out_ptr + offsets, 

125 q.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), 

126 mask=offsets < n_elements, 

127 ) 

128

130@triton.jit 

131def quantize_per_tensor_strided_kernel( 

132 x_ptr, 

133 out_ptr, 

134 inv_scale, 

135 zero_point, 

136 s0, 

137 s1, 

138 s2, 

139 s3, 

140 s4, 

141 s5, 

142 s6, 

143 s7, 

144 x0, 

145 x1, 

146 x2, 

147 x3, 

148 x4, 

149 x5, 

150 x6, 

151 x7, 

152 o0, 

153 o1, 

154 o2, 

155 o3, 

156 o4, 

157 o5, 

158 o6, 

159 o7, 

160 qmin: tl.constexpr, 

161 qmax: tl.constexpr, 

162 n_elements, 

163 ndim: tl.constexpr, 

164 IDX32: tl.constexpr, 

165 ALIGNED: tl.constexpr, 

166 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

167): 

168 """Same arithmetic as ``quantize_per_tensor_kernel``, but strided on both sides. 

169 

170 Used whenever the input and the destination do not share a linear memory 

171 order -- an ``out=`` in a non-contiguous layout (a slice, a transpose, a 

172 channels-last buffer) or a non-contiguous input. The flat kernel walks 

173 memory as a linear array, which only addresses the right elements when the 

174 logical order is the physical order; here the linear task index is instead 

175 decomposed into a multi-index against the *logical* shape and each side is 

176 re-flattened with its own strides. 

177 

178 The sizes and strides arrive as scalar arguments (``s0..s7``, ``x0..x7``, 

179 ``o0..o7``, padded with 1 up to ``MAX_NDIM`` = 8) rather than through 

180 pointer tensors: the wrapper then needs no per-call metadata allocations. 

181 

182 ``IDX32`` selects 32-bit index arithmetic; the launcher only sets it when 

183 the *whole span* of both sides fits int32, so the multiplication cannot 

184 overflow (see ``_int32_safe``). ``ALIGNED`` drops the boundary masks when 

185 the task count divides evenly into blocks (masked loads lower to 

186 per-element gathers on this backend). 

187 

188 Decomposition runs from the last dimension inward, the order a 

189 C-contiguous linear index is built in. Any order would be a valid 

190 bijection as long as both sides use the same one; this one is chosen so 

191 that for a contiguous destination the traversal matches the flat kernel's 

192 element for element. The shape is shared because both sides always have 

193 the input's shape (the ``out=`` path rejects a mismatch). 

194 """ 

195 pid = tl.program_id(axis=0) 

196 num_programs = tl.num_programs(axis=0) 

197 lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

198 n_blocks = tl.cdiv(n_elements, BLOCK_SIZE) 

199 for block in tl.range(pid, n_blocks, num_programs): 

200 offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + lane 

201 mask = offsets < n_elements 

202 if IDX32: 

203 src = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE], dtype=tl.int32) 

204 dst = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE], dtype=tl.int32) 

205 rem = offsets.to(tl.int32) 

206 else: 

207 src = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE], dtype=tl.int64) 

208 dst = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE], dtype=tl.int64) 

209 rem = offsets.to(tl.int64) 

210 for j in tl.static_range(ndim): 

211 k = ndim - 1 - j 

212 if k == 0: 

213 size, xst, ost = s0, x0, o0 

214 elif k == 1: 

215 size, xst, ost = s1, x1, o1 

216 elif k == 2: 

217 size, xst, ost = s2, x2, o2 

218 elif k == 3: 

219 size, xst, ost = s3, x3, o3 

220 elif k == 4: 

221 size, xst, ost = s4, x4, o4 

222 elif k == 5: 

223 size, xst, ost = s5, x5, o5 

224 elif k == 6: 

225 size, xst, ost = s6, x6, o6 

226 else: 

227 size, xst, ost = s7, x7, o7 

228 rem_col = rem % size 

229 src += rem_col * xst 

230 dst += rem_col * ost 

231 rem = rem // size 

232 if ALIGNED: 

233 x = tl.load(x_ptr + src) 

234 else: 

235 x = tl.load(x_ptr + src, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

236 q = tl_extra_shim.nearbyint(x * inv_scale) + zero_point 

237 q = tl.where(q == q, q, 0.0) 

238 q = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(q, qmin), qmax) 

239 if ALIGNED: 

240 tl.store(out_ptr + dst, q.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

241 else: 

242 tl.store(out_ptr + dst, q.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask) 

243 

244 

245# The stride arguments are padded to this many dimensions; a quantized CUDA 

246# tensor beyond 8 dimensions has no linear path anyway (``is_non_overlapping_ 

247# and_dense`` rejects it), so the strided kernel is the last resort and its 

248# argument list is bounded here. 

249MAX_NDIM = 8 

250 

251# 2**31 - 1, the largest value an int32 index can hold before the address 

252# arithmetic overflows. 

253_INT32_MAX = 2**31 - 1 

254 

255# Largest fp32 strictly below 2**31; clamping qint32 to this bound keeps the 

256# fp32 -> int32 narrowing in range (float(2**31 - 1) rounds up to 2**31, 

257# whose fptosi is undefined). 

258_F32_BELOW_INT32_MAX = 2147483520.0 

259 

260# The gcu400 backend rejects launches with grid.x above 65535; the kernels 

261# grid-stride over blocks so the launcher can cap the grid for large buffers. 

262_GRID_X_CAP = 65535 

263 

264 

265def _int32_safe(a, out_int): 

266 """True when every address either side touches fits in an int32 index.""" 

267 if a.numel() > _INT32_MAX or out_int.numel() > _INT32_MAX: 

268 return False 

269 

270 def span(shape, strides): 

271 return sum((size - 1) * stride for size, stride in zip(shape, strides)) 

272 

273 return ( 

274 span(a.shape, a.stride()) <= _INT32_MAX 

275 and span(out_int.shape, out_int.stride()) <= _INT32_MAX 

276 ) 

277 

278 

279def _padded(values, ndim): 

280 """Pad a shape/stride tuple with 1s up to ``MAX_NDIM`` dimensions.""" 

281 return tuple(values) + (1,) * (MAX_NDIM - ndim) 

282

284def _inv_scale_f32(scale): 

285 """fl32(1.0 / fl32(scale)) with torch's IEEE fp32 scalar division. 

286 

287 ATen's CPU quantizer computes ``inverse_scale = 1.0f / (float)scale``; 

288 reproducing the exact same fp32 reciprocal (torch scalar division is 

289 correctly rounded, unlike the backend's fast reciprocal) keeps the kernel 

290 bit-identical to the runnable CPU reference. Results are cached per scale. 

291 """ 

292 key = float(scale) 

293 cached = _INV_SCALE_CACHE.get(key) 

294 if cached is None: 

295 one = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32) 

296 s = torch.tensor(key, dtype=torch.float32) 

297 cached = float(one / s) 

298 _INV_SCALE_CACHE[key] = cached 

299 return cached 

300 

301 

302_INV_SCALE_CACHE = {} 

303 

304 

305def _f32_clamp_bounds(qmin, qmax): 

306 """Clamp bounds in the fp32 domain, kept inside the int32 representable range.""" 

307 return (float(qmin), min(float(qmax), _F32_BELOW_INT32_MAX))

322def _validate_quant_args(a, dtype): 

323 """ATen's input validation for the quantized dtype and the float input.""" 

324 if dtype not in _QUANT_INFO: 

325 raise RuntimeError( 

326 f"quantize_per_tensor: unsupported quantized dtype {dtype}, expected "

359def _per_tensor_affine_int(): 

360 """The raw ``QScheme`` integer for per-tensor affine. 

361 

362 ``torch.qscheme`` is an opaque wrapper (no ``int()``/``value``), while the 

363 ``qscheme`` redispatch returns the raw C++ integer the dispatcher boxes 

364 back into the wrapper; the canonical value is read once from a known 

365 per-tensor tensor so the two views can be compared. 

366 """ 

367 global _QSCHEME_PER_TENSOR_INT 

368 if _QSCHEME_PER_TENSOR_INT is None: 

369 known = _EMPTY_AFFINE_OP.redispatch( 

370 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

371 [1], 

372 dtype=torch.quint8, 

373 device=torch.device("cpu"), 

374 scale=1.0, 

375 zero_point=0, 

376 ) 

377 _QSCHEME_PER_TENSOR_INT = _QSCHEME_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, known) 

378 return _QSCHEME_PER_TENSOR_INT

381# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

382# GCU quantized-tensor platform layer. 

383# 

384# torch_gcu ships no kernels for the QuantizedPrivateUse1 ("Quantizedgcu") 

385# dispatch key, so every quantized op on a GCU tensor raises 

386# NotImplementedError. The helpers below restore the minimal surface this 

387# operator, its tests and its benchmarks need. Metadata-only ops (factories, 

388# accessors, set_/as_strided) redispatch to the QuantizedCPU registration, 

389# which is device-agnostic TensorImpl bookkeeping; data-moving ops are 

390# re-implemented over plain integer views so no CPU kernel ever touches GCU 

391# storage (redispatching those segfaults). Everything is installed through 

392# ``_install_gcu_quantized_platform`` at import time, exactly once per 

393# process (the backend loader imports this file under two module names, so 

394# the installed flag is anchored on the torch module, not this module). 

395# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

396_QCPU_KEYSET = torch._C.DispatchKeySet(torch._C.DispatchKey.QuantizedCPU) 

397_EMPTY_AFFINE_OP = torch.ops.aten._empty_affine_quantized.default 

398_EMPTY_PER_CHANNEL_OP = torch.ops.aten._empty_per_channel_affine_quantized.default 

399_QSCHEME_OP = torch.ops.aten.qscheme.default 

400_Q_SCALE_OP = torch.ops.aten.q_scale.default 

401_Q_ZERO_POINT_OP = torch.ops.aten.q_zero_point.default 

402_SET_STORAGE_OP = torch.ops.aten.set_.source_Storage_storage_offset 

403_AS_STRIDED_OP = torch.ops.aten.as_strided.default 

404 

405 

406def _empty_affine_quantized_on_device( 

407 size, scale, zero_point, dtype, device, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format 

408): 

409 """Allocate a per-tensor affine quantized tensor on any device. 

410 

411 The QuantizedCPU factory is device-generic: it allocates on the device its 

412 ``device`` argument names, so redispatching with device=gcu runs the native 

413 allocator exactly once (at::empty routes through BackendSelect to the gcu 

414 factory) while bypassing the missing Quantizedgcu entry. 

415 """ 

416 if isinstance(size, int): 

417 size = [size] 

418 elif isinstance(size, torch.Size): 

419 size = list(size) 

420 return _EMPTY_AFFINE_OP.redispatch( 

421 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

422 size, 

423 dtype=dtype, 

424 device=device, 

425 scale=float(scale), 

426 zero_point=int(zero_point), 

427 memory_format=memory_format, 

428 ) 

429 

430 

431def _empty_per_channel_quantized_on_device( 

432 size, scales, zero_points, axis, dtype, device 

433): 

434 if isinstance(size, torch.Size): 

435 size = list(size) 

436 return _EMPTY_PER_CHANNEL_OP.redispatch( 

437 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

438 size, 

439 scales=scales, 

440 zero_points=zero_points, 

441 axis=axis, 

442 dtype=dtype, 

443 device=device, 

444 )

447def _payload_view(qtensor, storage_dtype): 

448 """Alias a quantized tensor's storage as a plain integer tensor. 

449 

450 Plain-tensor ``set_`` dispatches under the (working) gcu key, so the view 

451 is writable by ordinary kernels whatever layout the quantized tensor has; 

452 the storage offset is part of ``data_ptr()``, so an offset view addresses 

453 its own slice. 

454 """ 

455 return torch.empty(0, dtype=storage_dtype, device=qtensor.device).set_( 

456 qtensor.untyped_storage(), 

457 qtensor.storage_offset(), 

458 tuple(qtensor.shape), 

459 qtensor.stride(), 

460 ) 

461 

462 

463def _quantizer_metadata(qtensor): 

464 return ( 

465 _QSCHEME_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, qtensor), 

466 _Q_SCALE_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, qtensor), 

467 _Q_ZERO_POINT_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, qtensor), 

468 )

483def _gcu_set_storage(self, source, storage_offset, size, stride=()):

489def _gcu_as_strided(self, size, stride, storage_offset=None): 

490 return _AS_STRIDED_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, self, size, stride, storage_offset)

493def _suggest_memory_format(t): 

494 """Mirror of ``TensorImpl::suggest_memory_format`` for the dense cases.""" 

495 if ( 

496 t.dim() == 4 

497 and t.shape[1] != 1 

498 and t.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last) 

499 ): 

500 return torch.channels_last 

501 if ( 

502 t.dim() == 5 

503 and t.shape[1] != 1 

504 and t.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d) 

505 ): 

506 return torch.channels_last_3d 

507 return torch.contiguous_format 

508 

509 

510def _gcu_int_repr(self): 

511 """``int_repr`` over plain integer views, preserving the dense layout. 

512 

513 The native op allocates its output with ``suggest_memory_format`` (dense 

514 permutation layouts are kept); the copy itself goes through ordinary 

515 strided tensor copies on the gcu key instead of the CPU kernel, which 

516 would dereference GCU storage through CPU pointers. 

517 """ 

518 storage_dtype = _QINT_DTYPES[self.dtype] 

519 view = _payload_view(self, storage_dtype) 

520 out = torch.empty( 

521 self.shape, 

522 dtype=storage_dtype, 

523 device=self.device, 

524 memory_format=_suggest_memory_format(self), 

525 ) 

526 out.copy_(view) 

527 return out 

528 

529 

530def _gcu_dequantize(self): 

531 scheme, scale, zero_point = _quantizer_metadata(self) 

532 if scheme != _per_tensor_affine_int(): 

533 raise NotImplementedError( 

534 "dequantize on the gcu backend supports per-tensor affine only" 

535 ) 

536 view = _payload_view(self, _QINT_DTYPES[self.dtype]) 

537 return (view.to(torch.float32) - zero_point) * scale 

538

540def _gcu_copy_from(self, dst, non_blocking=False): 

541 if _QSCHEME_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, self) != _QSCHEME_OP.redispatch( 

542 _QCPU_KEYSET, dst 

543 ): 

544 raise RuntimeError("Quantized Copy only works with same qscheme") 

545 src_storage = _QINT_DTYPES[self.dtype] 

546 dst_storage = _QINT_DTYPES[dst.dtype] 

547 if src_storage != dst_storage: 

548 raise RuntimeError( 

549 "Quantized Copy only works with same dtype: " 

550 f"expected {dst.dtype} but got {self.dtype}" 

551 ) 

552 dst_view = _payload_view(dst, dst_storage) 

553 src_view = _payload_view(self, src_storage) 

554 dst_view.copy_(src_view, non_blocking=non_blocking) 

555 return self 

556 

557 

558def _gcu_make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor(self, scale, zero_point): 

559 """Wrap a plain integer tensor's storage into a quantized tensor. 

560 

561 Pure TensorImpl work: allocate a 0-element quantized tensor with the 

562 requested quantizer, then repoint it at the source storage through the 

563 metadata ``set_`` redispatch. Sharing the caller's storage is the 

564 upstream contract (``int_repr()`` copies; this op must not). 

565 """ 

566 qdtype = _QDTYPE_FROM_INT.get(self.dtype) 

567 if qdtype is None: 

568 raise RuntimeError( 

569 f"_make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor: unsupported dtype {self.dtype}" 

570 ) 

571 fresh = _empty_affine_quantized_on_device(0, scale, zero_point, qdtype, self.device) 

572 _SET_STORAGE_OP.redispatch( 

573 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

574 fresh, 

575 self.untyped_storage(), 

576 self.storage_offset(), 

577 tuple(self.shape), 

578 self.stride(), 

579 ) 

580 return fresh 

581 

582

591 zero_point=0, 

592 memory_format=torch.contiguous_format, 

593): 

594 return _EMPTY_AFFINE_OP.redispatch( 

595 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

596 size, 

597 dtype=dtype, 

598 layout=layout, 

599 device=device,

601 scale=scale, 

602 zero_point=zero_point, 

603 memory_format=memory_format, 

604 )

633def _install_gcu_quantized_kernels(): 

634 """Register the QuantizedPrivateUse1 kernels (once per process). 

635 

636 Registration is fail-soft per op: sibling quantized operators in this 

637 backend family (max_pool, per-channel, ...) ship their own 

638 QuantizedPrivateUse1 bridges behind different install anchors, so once 

639 the patches are merged side by side the dispatcher may already hold a 

640 kernel for an op+key pair. Skipping keeps every patch loadable and leaves 

641 the first registrant active (the bridges are semantics-aligned family- 

642 wide; see the P21 dossier instances for the merge-order matrix). 

643 """ 

644 if getattr(torch, "_flaggems_gcu_quantize_platform", False): 

645 return 

646 lib = torch.library.Library("aten", "IMPL") 

647 registrations = ( 

648 ("qscheme", _gcu_qscheme), 

649 ("q_scale", _gcu_q_scale), 

650 ("q_zero_point", _gcu_q_zero_point), 

651 ("set_.source_Storage_storage_offset", _gcu_set_storage), 

652 ("as_strided", _gcu_as_strided), 

653 ("int_repr", _gcu_int_repr), 

654 ("dequantize.self", _gcu_dequantize), 

655 ("_copy_from", _gcu_copy_from), 

656 ("_empty_affine_quantized", _gcu_empty_affine_factory), 

657 ( 

658 "_empty_per_channel_affine_quantized", 

659 _gcu_empty_per_channel_factory, 

660 ), 

661 ("_make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor", _gcu_make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor), 

662 ) 

663 for name, impl in registrations: 

664 try: 

665 lib.impl(name, impl, "QuantizedPrivateUse1") 

666 except RuntimeError: 

667 logger.debug( 

668 "quantize_per_tensor: %s already registered on " 

669 "QuantizedPrivateUse1 by a sibling bridge; skipping", 

670 name, 

671 ) 

672 torch._flaggems_gcu_quantize_platform = lib 

673 

674 

675# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

676# Reference-arm shims (torch entry points). 

677# 

678# ``torch.quantize_per_tensor`` on a GCU tensor dies inside the aten composite 

679# (``empty_quantized`` under the missing Quantizedgcu key), so the accuracy 

680# suite has no reference. The shims below route GCU inputs through the CPU 

681# quantizer and rebuild the result on GCU with the same integer payload and 

682# quantizer, preserving the input's dense layout. While FlagGems' ``use_gems`` 

683# registration is active they pass through untouched, so dispatcher-level 

684# benchmark candidates still reach the registered FlagGems kernel instead of 

685# this reference path. 

686# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

687_ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR = None 

688_ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_CHANNEL = None 

689_ORIGINAL_EMPTY_AFFINE = None 

690_ORIGINAL_MAKE_PER_TENSOR = None 

691 

692 

693def _gems_registration_active(): 

694 try: 

695 import flag_gems 

696 

697 return flag_gems.current_work_registrar is not None 

698 except Exception: 

699 return False 

700 

701 

702def _resolve_gcu_device(device): 

703 """Map any cuda-flavoured device onto gcu; None when not accelerator-bound.""" 

704 if device is None: 

705 return None 

706 if isinstance(device, str): 

707 if device.startswith("cuda"): 

708 return torch.device("gcu" + device[4:]) 

709 if device.startswith("gcu"): 

710 return torch.device(device) 

711 return None 

712 if isinstance(device, torch.device): 

713 if device.type == "cuda": 

714 return torch.device("gcu", device.index) 

715 if device.type == "gcu": 

716 return device 

717 return None 

718 

719 

720def _rebuild_quantized_on_device(ref, device, scale, zero_point, dtype): 

721 """Rebuild a CPU quantized tensor on ``device`` with an identical payload.""" 

722 fresh = _empty_affine_quantized_on_device( 

723 tuple(ref.shape), 

724 scale, 

725 zero_point, 

726 dtype, 

727 device, 

728 memory_format=_suggest_memory_format(ref), 

729 ) 

730 if ref.numel() != 0: 

731 dst_view = _payload_view(fresh, _QINT_DTYPES[fresh.dtype]) 

732 dst_view.copy_(ref.int_repr()) 

733 return fresh 

734 

735 

736def _quantize_reference_on_device(input, scale, zero_point, dtype): 

737 input_cpu = input.detach().to("cpu") 

738 ref = _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR(input_cpu, scale, zero_point, dtype) 

739 return _rebuild_quantized_on_device(ref, input.device, scale, zero_point, dtype) 

740 

741 

742def _quantize_out_reference(input, scale, zero_point, dtype, out): 

743 result = _quantize_reference_on_device(input, scale, zero_point, dtype) 

744 if out.numel() != 0: 

745 dst_view = _payload_view(out, _QINT_DTYPES[out.dtype]) 

746 dst_view.copy_(result.int_repr()) 

747 if not _same_quantizer(out, scale, zero_point): 

748 _adopt_quantizer(out, scale, zero_point) 

749 return out 

750 

751 

752def _install_reference_shims(): 

753 global _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR, _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_CHANNEL 

754 global _ORIGINAL_EMPTY_AFFINE, _ORIGINAL_MAKE_PER_TENSOR 

755 

756 quantize = torch.quantize_per_tensor 

757 if not getattr(quantize, "_flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref", False): 

758 _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR = quantize 

759 

760 def _quantize_safe( 

761 input, scale=None, zero_point=None, dtype=None, *args, **kwargs 

762 ): 

763 if ( 

764 _is_gcu_tensor(input) 

765 and scale is not None 

766 and zero_point is not None 

767 and dtype is not None 

768 and not _gems_registration_active() 

769 ): 

770 return _quantize_reference_on_device(input, scale, zero_point, dtype) 

771 return _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR( 

772 input, scale, zero_point, dtype, *args, **kwargs 

773 ) 

774 

775 _quantize_safe._flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref = True 

776 torch.quantize_per_tensor = _quantize_safe 

777 

778 per_channel = torch.quantize_per_channel 

779 if not getattr(per_channel, "_flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref", False): 

780 _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_CHANNEL = per_channel 

781 

782 def _per_channel_safe( 

783 input, scales, zero_points, axis, dtype=None, *args, **kwargs 

784 ): 

785 if _is_gcu_tensor(input) and not _gems_registration_active(): 

786 ref = _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_CHANNEL( 

787 input.detach().to("cpu"), 

788 scales.detach().to("cpu"), 

789 zero_points.detach().to("cpu"), 

790 axis, 

791 dtype, 

792 ) 

793 fresh = _empty_per_channel_quantized_on_device( 

794 tuple(ref.shape), scales, zero_points, axis, dtype, input.device 

795 ) 

796 if ref.numel() != 0: 

797 dst_view = _payload_view(fresh, _QINT_DTYPES[fresh.dtype]) 

798 dst_view.copy_(ref.int_repr()) 

799 return fresh 

800 return _ORIGINAL_QUANTIZE_PER_CHANNEL( 

801 input, scales, zero_points, axis, dtype, *args, **kwargs 

802 ) 

803 

804 _per_channel_safe._flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref = True 

805 torch.quantize_per_channel = _per_channel_safe 

806 

807 empty_affine = torch._empty_affine_quantized 

808 if not getattr(empty_affine, "_flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref", False): 

809 _ORIGINAL_EMPTY_AFFINE = empty_affine 

810 

811 def _empty_affine_safe( 

812 size, 

813 *, 

814 dtype=None, 

815 layout=None, 

816 device=None, 

817 pin_memory=None, 

818 scale=1.0, 

819 zero_point=0, 

820 memory_format=torch.contiguous_format, 

821 ): 

822 gcu_device = _resolve_gcu_device(device) 

823 if gcu_device is not None: 

824 return _empty_affine_quantized_on_device( 

825 size, scale, zero_point, dtype, gcu_device, memory_format 

826 ) 

827 return _ORIGINAL_EMPTY_AFFINE( 

828 size, 

829 dtype=dtype, 

830 layout=layout, 

831 device=device, 

832 pin_memory=pin_memory, 

833 scale=scale, 

834 zero_point=zero_point, 

835 memory_format=memory_format, 

836 ) 

837 

838 _empty_affine_safe._flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref = True 

839 torch._empty_affine_quantized = _empty_affine_safe 

840 

841 make_per_tensor = torch._make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor 

842 if not getattr(make_per_tensor, "_flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref", False): 

843 _ORIGINAL_MAKE_PER_TENSOR = make_per_tensor 

844 

845 def _make_per_tensor_safe(self, scale, zero_point): 

846 if _is_gcu_tensor(self): 

847 return _gcu_make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor(self, scale, zero_point) 

848 return _ORIGINAL_MAKE_PER_TENSOR(self, scale, zero_point) 

849 

850 _make_per_tensor_safe._flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref = True 

851 torch._make_per_tensor_quantized_tensor = _make_per_tensor_safe 

852 

853 packet = torch.ops.aten.quantize_per_tensor 

854 for overload_name in ("default", "out"): 

855 overload = getattr(packet, overload_name, None) 

856 if overload is None or getattr(overload, "_flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref", False): 

857 continue 

858 is_out = overload_name == "out" 

859 

860 def _make_safe(overload, is_out): 

861 def _safe_overload(*args, **kwargs): 

862 input = args[0] if args else kwargs.get("input") 

863 if input is None: 

864 input = kwargs.get("self") 

865 scale = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else kwargs.get("scale") 

866 zero_point = args[2] if len(args) > 2 else kwargs.get("zero_point") 

867 dtype = args[3] if len(args) > 3 else kwargs.get("dtype") 

868 out = kwargs.get("out") 

869 if ( 

870 _is_gcu_tensor(input) 

871 and scale is not None 

872 and zero_point is not None 

873 and dtype is not None 

874 and not _gems_registration_active() 

875 ): 

876 if is_out and out is not None: 

877 return _quantize_out_reference( 

878 input, scale, zero_point, dtype, out 

879 ) 

880 return _quantize_reference_on_device( 

881 input, scale, zero_point, dtype 

882 ) 

883 return overload(*args, **kwargs) 

884 

885 _safe_overload._flaggems_gcu_quantize_ref = True 

886 return _safe_overload 

887 

888 try: 

889 setattr(packet, overload_name, _make_safe(overload, is_out)) 

890 except (AttributeError, TypeError): 

891 logger.debug("aten quantize_per_tensor.%s shim unavailable", overload_name) 

892 

893 

894def _install_gcu_quantized_platform(): 

895 # torch_gcu's transfer layer completes several device translations 

896 # (torch.Tensor.cuda, torch.empty's device argument, torch.Generator) 

897 # lazily; until it runs, ``device='cuda'`` constructions raise "Torch not 

898 # compiled with CUDA enabled" non-deterministically mid-session. Running 

899 # the availability probe once here makes the state deterministic for 

900 # every later import and test order. 

901 try: 

902 torch.cuda.is_available() 

903 except Exception: 

904 pass 

905 _install_gcu_quantized_kernels() 

906 _install_reference_shims() 

907 

908 

909# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

910# Launcher. 

911# 

912# The kernels are resolved through the *generic* module's namespace at call 

913# time. Two reasons: the accuracy suite monkeypatches 

914# ``flag_gems.ops.quantize_per_tensor.quantize_per_tensor_kernel`` (it cannot 

915# see this backend copy) to count Triton launches, and it also calls the 

916# generic ``_quantize_per_tensor_impl`` directly. Injecting the GCU-safe 

917# kernels and this launcher into that namespace makes both introspection 

918# points observe the kernels that actually run, without touching the generic 

919# file (on non-enflame hosts this module is never loaded). 

920# 

921# ``importlib.import_module`` is required to reach the module object itself: 

922# ``import flag_gems.ops.quantize_per_tensor as x`` binds ``x`` to the 

923# *function* of the same name, because ``flag_gems/ops/__init__.py`` re-exports 

924# it and thereby shadows the submodule attribute on the package. 

925# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

926import importlib as _importlib # noqa: E402 

927 

928_generic_impl = _importlib.import_module("flag_gems.ops.quantize_per_tensor") 

929 

930 

931def _launch_quantize_kernel(a, out_int, scale, zero_point, qmin, qmax): 

932 """Run the quantization kernel, writing ``out_int`` through its own layout.""" 

933 n_elements = out_int.numel() 

934 if n_elements == 0: 

935 return out_int 

936 inv_scale = _inv_scale_f32(scale) 

937 qmin_f, qmax_f = _f32_clamp_bounds(qmin, qmax) 

938 # Block / warp sweet spot measured across the benchmark's core shapes 

939 # (1M-537M elements): BLOCK=4096 with num_warps=2 reaches 185-251 GB/s 

940 # for this 4-byte-read / 1-byte-write element (BLOCK=1024 caps at ~77 

941 # GB/s; wider blocks over-subscribe and dip past 16384). Small buffers 

942 # are launch-bound and insensitive. 

943 BLOCK_SIZE = 4096 

944 num_warps = 2 

945 # Drop the boundary masks when the task count divides evenly into blocks: 

946 # masked loads lower to per-element gathers on this backend even when the 

947 # mask is runtime-true. 

948 aligned = n_elements % BLOCK_SIZE == 0 

949 # Cap the launch grid at the backend's grid.x hardware limit; the kernels 

950 # are grid-stride, so a capped grid still covers every block. 

951 programs = min(triton.cdiv(n_elements, BLOCK_SIZE), _GRID_X_CAP) 

952 grid = (programs,) 

953 if _linear_layout(a, out_int): 

954 _generic_impl.quantize_per_tensor_kernel[grid]( 

955 a, 

956 out_int, 

957 inv_scale, 

958 int(zero_point), 

959 qmin=qmin_f, 

960 qmax=qmax_f, 

961 n_elements=n_elements, 

962 ALIGNED=aligned, 

963 BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE, 

964 num_warps=num_warps, 

965 ) 

966 else: 

967 ndim = out_int.dim() 

968 if ndim > MAX_NDIM: 

969 raise RuntimeError( 

970 f"quantize_per_tensor: inputs with more than {MAX_NDIM} dimensions " 

971 f"are not supported, got {ndim}" 

972 ) 

973 _generic_impl.quantize_per_tensor_strided_kernel[grid]( 

974 a, 

975 out_int, 

976 inv_scale, 

977 int(zero_point), 

978 *_padded(out_int.shape, ndim), 

979 *_padded(a.stride(), ndim), 

980 *_padded(out_int.stride(), ndim), 

981 qmin=qmin_f, 

982 qmax=qmax_f, 

983 n_elements=n_elements, 

984 ndim=ndim, 

985 IDX32=_int32_safe(a, out_int), 

986 ALIGNED=aligned, 

987 BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE, 

988 num_warps=num_warps, 

989 ) 

990 return out_int 

991 

992 

993_generic_impl.quantize_per_tensor_kernel = quantize_per_tensor_kernel 

994_generic_impl.quantize_per_tensor_strided_kernel = quantize_per_tensor_strided_kernel 

995_generic_impl._launch_quantize_kernel = _launch_quantize_kernel 

996 

997 

998def _int_view(qtensor): 

999 """Alias a quantized tensor's storage as a writable integer tensor.""" 

1000 return _payload_view(qtensor, _QINT_DTYPES[qtensor.dtype]) 

1001 

1002 

1003def _aliases(a, out): 

1004 """True when ``out`` shares storage with the float input ``a``.""" 

1005 return out.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == a.untyped_storage().data_ptr() 

1006 

1007 

1008def _same_quantizer(out, scale, zero_point): 

1009 """True when ``out`` already carries this per-tensor quantizer.""" 

1010 return ( 

1011 _QSCHEME_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, out) == _per_tensor_affine_int() 

1012 and _Q_SCALE_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, out) == float(scale) 

1013 and _Q_ZERO_POINT_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, out) == int(zero_point) 

1014 ) 

1015 

1016 

1017def _adopt_quantizer(out, scale, zero_point): 

1018 """Re-point ``out`` at ``scale`` / ``zero_point``, in place, without copying. 

1019 

1020 The values are written by the kernel, so only the quantizer needs to move: 

1021 a ``.data`` assignment of an alias that shares ``out``'s storage, offset, 

1022 sizes and strides swaps it while leaving the tensor's storage, layout and 

1023 identity untouched. The alias is built with the QuantizedCPU factory (which 

1024 allocates on the named device) plus the metadata ``set_`` redispatch. 

1025 """ 

1026 alias = _empty_affine_quantized_on_device( 

1027 0, scale, zero_point, out.dtype, out.device 

1028 ) 

1029 _SET_STORAGE_OP.redispatch( 

1030 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

1031 alias, 

1032 out.untyped_storage(), 

1033 out.storage_offset(), 

1034 tuple(out.shape), 

1035 out.stride(), 

1036 ) 

1037 out.data = alias 

1038 return out 

1039 

1040 

1041def _copy_int(dst_int, src_int): 

1042 """Copy integers device-side, honouring both sides' strides.""" 

1043 from flag_gems.runtime.backend._enflame.gcu400.ops.copy import copy_ 

1044 

1045 copy_(dst_int, src_int) 

1046 return dst_int 

1047 

1048 

1049def _linear_layout(a, out_int): 

1050 """True when a flat element index addresses the same physical slot on both sides.""" 

1051 return ( 

1052 a.stride() == out_int.stride() 

1053 and torch.ops.aten.is_non_overlapping_and_dense(a) 

1054 ) 

1055 

1056 

1057def _quantize_per_tensor_impl(a, scale, zero_point, dtype): 

1058 """Shared core: compute the quantized integer representation of ``a``. 

1059 

1060 Returns the integer storage tensor (e.g. uint8 for quint8) holding 

1061 ``clamp(nearbyint(x * inv_scale) + zero_point, qmin, qmax)``. 

1062 """ 

1063 storage_dtype, qmin, qmax = _validate_quant_args(a, dtype) 

1064 

1065 memory_format = _suggest_memory_format(a) 

1066 if memory_format is torch.contiguous_format or a.dim() < 4: 

1067 out = torch.empty(a.shape, dtype=storage_dtype, device=a.device) 

1068 a = a.contiguous() 

1069 else: 

1070 out = torch.empty( 

1071 a.shape, dtype=storage_dtype, device=a.device, memory_format=memory_format 

1072 ) 

1073 a = a.contiguous(memory_format=memory_format) 

1074 return _launch_quantize_kernel(a, out, scale, zero_point, qmin, qmax) 

1075 

1076 

1077def _make_per_tensor_from_int(int_repr, scale, zero_point): 

1078 """Wrap ``int_repr`` as a per-tensor quantized tensor, preserving its layout.""" 

1079 result = _empty_affine_quantized_on_device( 

1080 0, scale, zero_point, _QDTYPE_FROM_INT[int_repr.dtype], int_repr.device 

1081 ) 

1082 _SET_STORAGE_OP.redispatch( 

1083 _QCPU_KEYSET, 

1084 result, 

1085 int_repr.untyped_storage(), 

1086 int_repr.storage_offset(), 

1087 tuple(int_repr.shape), 

1088 int_repr.stride(), 

1089 ) 

1090 return result 

1091 

1092 

1093def quantize_per_tensor(a, scale, zero_point, dtype): 

1094 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR") 

1095 _check_zero_point_range(zero_point, dtype) 

1096 int_repr = _quantize_per_tensor_impl(a, scale, zero_point, dtype) 

1097 return _make_per_tensor_from_int(int_repr, float(scale), int(zero_point)) 

1098 

1099 

1100def quantize_per_tensor_out(a, scale, zero_point, dtype, *, out=None): 

1101 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 QUANTIZE_PER_TENSOR_OUT") 

1102 _check_zero_point_range(zero_point, dtype) 

1103 if out is None: 

1104 raise RuntimeError("quantize_per_tensor.out: argument 'out' is required") 

1105 

1106 if out.dtype != dtype: 

1107 raise RuntimeError( 

1108 f"Expected out tensor to have dtype {dtype}, but got {out.dtype} instead" 

1109 ) 

1110 if out.device != a.device: 

1111 raise RuntimeError( 

1112 f"Expected out tensor to have device {a.device}, but got {out.device} " 

1113 "instead" 

1114 ) 

1115 if tuple(out.shape) != tuple(a.shape): 

1116 raise RuntimeError( 

1117 f"quantize_per_tensor.out: out has shape {tuple(out.shape)} but the " 

1118 f"result requires {tuple(a.shape)}; resizing a quantized CUDA output " 

1119 "is not supported" 

1120 ) 

1121 storage_dtype, qmin, qmax = _validate_quant_args(a, dtype) 

1122 

1123 if _QSCHEME_OP.redispatch(_QCPU_KEYSET, out) != _per_tensor_affine_int(): 

1124 raise RuntimeError("Quantized Copy only works with same qscheme") 

1125 

1126 if has_internal_overlapping(out) == MemOverlap.Yes: 

1127 raise RuntimeError( 

1128 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the written-to " 

1129 "tensor refers to a single memory location. Please clone() the " 

1130 "tensor before performing the operation." 

1131 ) 

1132 

1133 if _aliases(a, out):
